summary: Generation-atomic cloud save (envelope v3): new pushes write chunks under generation-isolated keys nd_<gen>_<i> that never touch the committed generation's keys; nd_meta stays the atomic commit-pointer (written strictly last, {v:3,g,n,t,c,id,sz,prev}); CAS re-read before the meta write aborts our push when a concurrent writer committed a newer generation (conflict surfaces as err.conflict, own chunks cleaned, theirs left current); the reader rolls back to meta.prev (depth 1) when the committed generation is corrupt, keeping the legacy flat nd_<i> read path for envelopes <= v2 (first v3 commit over a legacy cloud keeps nd_0..n-1 as the rollback copy and sweeps surplus); saveToCloud now uses the same atomic core (no flat writes anywhere); resetAllData wipes the cloud by last-known generation descriptors; fault injection hooks per chunk/meta/concurrent writer (ND_CLOUD_FAULTS, always null in production) drive the new contract tests; TELEMETRY.md and the neurodeck-data-sync skill document the v3 envelope, new telemetry events/codes, and the revised nd_0 contracts (regression-T5M1, e2e T1-H3); runtime pins bumped 103->104 (index.html ?v=104 x15, sw.js nd-shell-v104) with exact assertions repinned.

tests.command: node --test tests/cloud-envelope.test.js tests/cloud-generation.test.js tests/recovery-cloud.test.js tests/integration.test.js tests/regression-T5M1-quota-chain.test.js

limitations: Physical device tests TBD (real Telegram CloudStorage client behavior verified only via contract stubs and browser e2e with stubbed CloudStorage).

Old cached app versions (shell <= v103) read a v3 cloud as corrupt and fall back to local/IDB layers; no data loss, fresh client reads everything - documented in docs/operations/TELEMETRY.md section 6.
Writer conflict detection is best-effort CAS (re-read before commit), not a cloud-side atomic compare-and-swap; Telegram CloudStorage has no CAS primitive.
Driver runs the full 9-step CI (npm run ci) after exit; this package ran check:js, narrow cloud tests, full unit suite, affected e2e files, and qa:data.
